runs.title: Madueke on Mac Allister: what actually happened
runs.prompt: Chelsea's Noni Madueke is trending for saying Liverpool's Alexis Mac Allister tried to bait him into a red card. Find out what actually happened: what Madueke said, what the incident was during the match, and whether either club or player has responded. Use a readable (non-paywalled) sports news source.
runs.answer: Quick correction first: Noni Madueke is no longer Chelsea's — he's an Arsenal player (he joined in July 2025), and the incident happened in Arsenal's 1-0 win at Liverpool on 1 November 2026 (Kai Havertz's goal). After Mac Allister shoved/struck a grounded Martin Odegaard, a melee followed and Madueke and Mac Allister went head-to-head, their heads touching slightly; Mac Allister went down theatrically, but referee Andy Madley gave no red and VAR (Stuart Attwell) backed him. Speaking to Viaplay's Freddie Ljungberg, Madueke said: "I don't think it's anything whether it's a yellow card or a red card... It's a natural movement. He's obviously clever, he tried to bait me into getting a red card there, but obviously not," adding he was thinking about VAR at the time, and joking he wished he'd swapped shirts with Mac Allister. I found no on-record response from Mac Allister, Liverpool or Arsenal to the "bait" claim itself — only Mikel Arteta defending his side in the wider refereeing row over shirt-pulls/penalties, and ex-referees criticising both players for "tarnishing the image" of the league.

Document exactly what you can and cannot see — the wall you hit is the whole point of this task.
runs.answer: Instagram's topic pages ARE readable without logging in, and they confirm the release: Trader Joe's mystery packs return in "early November 2026" at $2.99, each brown-paper bundle holding three six-gallon reusable bags with exclusive/regional designs not sold separately — but every page's "Sources" summary is CSS-clamped and ends in "… more" exactly where the design names would be (one variant literally reads "Two designs in this year's … more"). The 2026 design names are therefore NOT retrievable: the feed of 8 posts on /popular/trader-joes-mystery-bags-2026/ shows only handle, verified badge, view count (e.g. andiekallred 475K, maddiedidwhatt 3.9K, fomomommy 4.2K), caption text and hashtags — no thumbnails, no alt text, no playable reels, no post permalinks, so the "unboxing" visuals can't be seen at all. Captions only hint at designs generically ("guess all 3 states," "a regional favorite or a rare print," Nebraska/New Jersey/Wisconsin/Maryland/Alabama/Oklahoma, "I think I got another rare one this year"), and Instagram's profile, hashtag and explore surfaces hard-redirect to /accounts/login. Bottom line: the text facts are free, the designs are behind the login wall.
obstacles: Topic-page 'Sources' blurb is CSS-clamped at '... more', cutting off the 2026 design names — no expand control reachable without JS/login
No image content or alt text served to a non-logged-in GET, so bag designs and unboxing visuals are entirely invisible
